pairs.source_text: Domitianus natus est VIIII. Kal. Novemb. patre consule designato inituroque mense insequenti honorem, regione urbis sexta ad Malum Punicum, domo quam postea in templum gentis Flaviae convertit.
pairs.question: Quo die natum esse Domitianum Suetonius tradit?
pairs.answer: Ante diem nonum Kalendas Novembres (VIIII Kal. Novemb.).
pairs.question_en: On what day does Suetonius say Domitian was born?
pairs.answer_en: On the ninth day before the Kalends of November (24 October).
pairs.derivation: Birth-date fact, anchored to Domitian. Supported verbatim by 'Domitianus natus est VIIII. Kal. Novemb.' Indirect statement (natum esse) under tradit. Closed-book: the birth-date (24 October AD 51) of a major emperor; short calendrical answer.

pairs.source_text: regione urbis sexta ad Malum Punicum, domo quam postea in templum gentis Flaviae convertit.
pairs.question: In quod templum Domitianus domum, in qua natus erat, postea convertit?
pairs.question_en: Into what temple did Domitian later convert the house in which he had been born?
pairs.answer_en: Into the temple of the Flavian gens.
pairs.derivation: Building/family fact: Domitian's birth-house (in Rome's sixth region) was later turned into the Templum Gentis Flaviae, the dynastic shrine of the Flavians. Supported verbatim by 'domo quam postea in templum gentis Flaviae convertit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian; single named-monument answer.

pairs.source_text: contrectatis multorum uxoribus, Domitiam Longinam Aelio Lamiae nuptam etiam in matrimonium abduxit, atque uno die super XX. officia urbana aut peregrina distribuit.
pairs.question: Quam feminam, Aelio Lamiae nuptam, Domitianus in matrimonium abduxit?
pairs.question_en: Which woman, married to Aelius Lamia, did Domitian carry off into marriage?
pairs.derivation: Family fact: Domitian's wife was Domitia Longina, whom he took from her husband Aelius Lamia. Supported verbatim by 'Domitiam Longinam Aelio Lamiae nuptam etiam in matrimonium abduxit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + Aelius Lamia; single-name answer; closed-book (Domitia Longina, daughter of Corbulo, is the well-known empress).

pairs.source_text: habitabat cum patre una, sellamque eius ac fratris, quotiens prodirent, lectica sequebatur ac triumphum utriusque Iudaicum equo albo comitatus est.
pairs.question: Quo equo Domitianus triumphum Iudaicum patris fratrisque comitatus est?
pairs.question_en: On what horse did Domitian accompany the Jewish triumph of his father and brother?
pairs.derivation: Career detail: Domitian rode a white horse in the Jewish triumph of his father Vespasian and brother Titus (AD 71). Supported verbatim by 'triumphum utriusque Iudaicum equo albo comitatus est.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + the Jewish triumph; short, concrete answer.

pairs.source_text: nec quicquam amplius quam muscas captare ac stilo praeacuto configere; ut cuidam interroganti, essetne quis intus cum Caesare, non absurde responsum sit a Vibio Crispo, ne muscam quidem.
pairs.question: Quid Vibius Crispus respondit interroganti num quis intus cum Domitiano esset?
pairs.question_en: What did Vibius Crispus reply to the man who asked whether anyone was inside with Domitian?
pairs.derivation: Famous joke: Domitian spent his hours stabbing flies, so when asked if anyone was with Caesar, Vibius Crispus quipped 'not even a fly.' Supported verbatim. Entity-anchored to Vibius Crispus + Domitian; the witticism survives translation; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Instituit et quinquennale certamen Capitolino Iovi triplex, musicum, equestre, gymnicum, et aliquanto plurium quam nunc est coronatorum.
pairs.question: In cuius dei honorem Domitianus quinquennale certamen triplex instituit?
pairs.question_en: In whose honor did Domitian establish a triple quinquennial contest?
pairs.derivation: Institutional fact: Domitian founded the quinquennial Capitoline Games (musical, equestrian, gymnastic) in honor of Capitoline Jupiter. Supported verbatim by 'quinquennale certamen Capitolino Iovi triplex.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + Capitoline Jupiter; single-name answer; the Agon Capitolinus is a recognized institution.

pairs.source_text: De Chattis Dacisque post varia proelia duplicem triumphum egit.
pairs.question: De quibus gentibus Domitianus duplicem triumphum egit?
pairs.question_en: Over which peoples did Domitian celebrate a double triumph?
pairs.answer_en: Over the Chatti and the Dacians.
pairs.derivation: Military fact: a double triumph over the Chatti and the Dacians. Supported verbatim by 'De Chattis Dacisque ... duplicem triumphum egit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + named peoples; short list answer.

pairs.source_text: Bellum civile motum a L. Antonio, superioris Germaniae praeside, confecit absens felicitate mira.
pairs.question: Quis, superioris Germaniae praeses, bellum civile adversus Domitianum movit?
pairs.question_en: Who, as governor of Upper Germany, stirred up civil war against Domitian?
pairs.derivation: Historical fact: the revolt of L. Antonius Saturninus, governor of Upper Germany (AD 89), put down in Domitian's absence. Supported verbatim by 'Bellum civile motum a L. Antonio, superioris Germaniae praeside.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + the office; single-name answer (cognomen Saturninus supplied only in the gloss, not the text).

pairs.source_text: Iunium Rusticum, quod Paeti Thraseae et Helvidii Prisci laudes edidisset appellassetque eos sanctissimos viros; cuius criminis occasione philosophos omnis urbe Italiaque summovit.
pairs.question: Quos Domitianus, occasione damnati Iunii Rustici, urbe Italiaque summovit?
pairs.question_en: Whom did Domitian expel from Rome and Italy, on the occasion of the condemnation of Junius Rusticus?
pairs.derivation: Historical fact: Domitian's expulsion of philosophers from Rome and Italy, occasioned by the condemnation of Junius Rusticus (who had praised Thrasea Paetus and Helvidius Priscus). Supported verbatim by 'philosophos omnis urbe Italiaque summovit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian + Junius Rusticus; short answer; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Pari arrogantia, cum procuratorum suorum nomine formalem dictaret epistulam, sic coepit: "Dominus et deus noster hoc fieri iubet." Vnde institutum posthac, ut ne scripto quidem ac sermone cuiusquam appellaretur aliter.
pairs.question: Quibus verbis se appellari Domitianus voluit, cum epistulam procuratorum suorum nomine dictaret?
pairs.question_en: By what words did Domitian want himself to be addressed, when he dictated a letter in the name of his procurators?
pairs.derivation: Iconic fact: Domitian had himself styled 'dominus et deus,' beginning an official letter 'Our lord and god orders this,' and thereafter was addressed no otherwise. Supported verbatim. Entity-anchored to Domitian; the title survives translation; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Consulatus septemdecim cepit, quot ante eum nemo; ex quibus septem medios continuavit, omnes autem paene titulo tenus gessit.
pairs.question: Quot consulatus Domitianus cepit, quot ante eum nemo gesserat?
pairs.question_en: How many consulships did Domitian hold, more than anyone before him?
pairs.derivation: Number fact: Domitian held seventeen consulships, more than any predecessor. Supported verbatim by 'Consulatus septemdecim cepit, quot ante eum nemo.' Entity-anchored to Domitian; single-number answer; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Post autem duos triumphos Germanici cognomine assumpto Septembrem mensem et Octobrem ex appellationibus suis Germanico Domitianumque transnominavit, quod altero suscepisset imperium, altero natus esset.
pairs.question: In quae nomina Domitianus menses Septembrem et Octobrem transnominavit?
pairs.answer: Septembrem in Germanicum, Octobrem in Domitianum.
pairs.question_en: Into what names did Domitian rename the months of September and October?
pairs.derivation: Naming fact: Domitian renamed September 'Germanicus' (the month he had taken up the empire) and October 'Domitianus' (the month he was born). Supported verbatim by 'Septembrem mensem et Octobrem ... Germanico Domitianumque transnominavit.' Entity-anchored to Domitian; short paired answer; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Per haec terribilis cunctis et invisus, tandem oppressus est amicorum libertorumque intimorum conspiratione, simul et uxoris.
pairs.question: Qua coniuratione Domitianus tandem oppressus est?
pairs.answer: Amicorum libertorumque intimorum, simul et uxoris.
pairs.question_en: By what conspiracy was Domitian at last overthrown?
pairs.answer_en: By a conspiracy of his intimate friends and freedmen, together with his wife.
pairs.derivation: Death fact: Domitian was killed by a palace conspiracy of his closest friends and freedmen, joined by his wife. Supported verbatim by 'oppressus est amicorum libertorumque intimorum conspiratione, simul et uxoris.' Entity-anchored to Domitian; short phrase answer; closed-book (the assassination of AD 96).

pairs.source_text: Stephanus, Domitillae procurator, et tunc interceptarum pecuniarum reus, consilium operamque optulit. Ac sinisteriore brachio, velut aegro, lanis fasciisque per aliquot dies ad avertendam suspicionem obvoluto, ad ipsam horam dolorem interiecit; professusque conspirationis indicium et ob hos admissus, legenti traditum a se libellum et attonito suffodit inguina.
pairs.question: Quis Domitiano, legenti libellum, primum vulnus intulit, inguina suffodiens?
pairs.question_en: Who struck the first blow at Domitian, stabbing him in the groin while he read a document?
pairs.derivation: Assassination fact: the steward Stephanus struck the first blow, stabbing Domitian in the groin as he read a handed-over document. Supported verbatim by 'Stephanus, Domitillae procurator ... legenti traditum a se libellum et attonito suffodit inguina.' Entity-anchored; single-name answer; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Occisus est XIIII. Kal. Octob. anno aetatis quadragensimo quinto, imperii quinto decimo.
pairs.question: Quotum aetatis annum agens Domitianus occisus est?
pairs.question_en: In which year of his age was Domitian killed?
pairs.derivation: Age-at-death fact. Supported verbatim by 'anno aetatis quadragensimo quinto.' Ordinal/number answer, entity-anchored to Domitian; closed-book (killed AD 96, aged 44/45). Source retains the Latin Library spelling 'quadragensimo' for 'quadragesimo.'

pairs.source_text: Occisus est XIIII. Kal. Octob. anno aetatis quadragensimo quinto, imperii quinto decimo.
pairs.question: Quoto imperii anno Domitianus occisus est?
pairs.question_en: In which year of his reign was Domitian killed?
pairs.derivation: Reign-length fact: Domitian was killed in the fifteenth year of his reign (AD 81-96). Supported verbatim by 'imperii quinto decimo.' Ordinal/number answer, entity-anchored to Domitian; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Contra senatus adeo laetatus est, ut repleta certatim curia non temperaret, quin mortuum contumeliosissimo atque acerbissimo adclamationum genere laceraret, scalas etiam inferri clipeosque et imagines eius coram detrahi et ibidem solo affligi iuberet, novissime eradendos ubique titulos abolendamque omnes memoriam decerneret.
pairs.question: Quid senatus de Domitiano occiso decrevit, titulos eius ubique eradi iubens?
pairs.question_en: What did the senate decree about the slain Domitian, ordering his inscriptions to be erased everywhere?
pairs.answer_en: That all memory of him be abolished (the damnatio memoriae).
pairs.derivation: Historical fact: the senate rejoiced at Domitian's death and decreed his inscriptions erased and all memory of him abolished (damnatio memoriae). Supported verbatim by 'novissime eradendos ubique titulos abolendamque omnes memoriam decerneret.' Entity-anchored to the senate + Domitian; short noun-phrase answer; closed-book.
